BETWEEN:-
 MOHAMMAD SHAFIQ KHAN S/O BAANTE KHAN, AGED  38 YEARS, R/O WARD NO. 4 POLICE STATION PHOOP,
 DISTRICT BHIND (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI RAVINDRA SINGH KUSHWAH - ADVOCATE)
 AND  STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH POLICE  STATION PHOOP, DISTRICT BHIND (MADHYA  PRADESH)
 .
 (BY SHRI A.P.S. TOMAR - PUBLIC PROSECUTOR)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the c  following:
 ORDER Case diary is available.
With the consent, heard finally.

This is second application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C for grant of bail to the applicant as he has been arrested on 1.12.2022 in connection with Crime No.262/2022 registered at Police Station Phoop, District Bhind for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(n), 506 of IPC and under Sections 67, 67A of I.T. Act.
First application was dismissed as withdrawn by order dated 30.1.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.62116/2022.

Prosecution story, in brief is that in between 1.9.2022 to 23.11.2022 when complainant/prosecutrix was going to deliver the meal to her husband and reached near the house of Jitendra, then the Mohammad Shafiq Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22806897/
1 applicant forcibly took her in an abundant house situated in front of Jitendra's house, threatened her and committed rape upon her.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He also made video recording of rape and thereafter called her again and committed rape upon her and threatened that he will viral her video.
Thereafter, he gave the aforesaid video to co-accused Mohd. Arif who made the same viral.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that prosecutrix is a major married lady aged about 40 years having three children.
As per prosecution case itself, she did not report the matter to the police prior to lodging of the FIR i.e. 30.11.2022.
During trial, her statements have been recorded wherein she deposed that the applicant along with other co-accused persons forcibly took her in an abundant house and committed mass rape upon her.
Her statements are inconsistent with regard to the incident.
No injury was found on her body.
She was a consenting party.
Her statement has been recorded.
Trial will take time to conclude and the co-accused has already been enlarged on bail by the Trial Court and therefore, in the aforesaid circumstances, applicant is entitled for grant of bail.
Learned counsel for the respondent/State has vehemently opposed the prayer and submits that the the allegations against the applicant are of serious in nature.
He is main accused in the matter.
His case is entirely different from the case of co-accused, therefore, the applicant is not entitled to be enlarged on bail.
Heard the learned counsel for both the parties.

Having considered rival submission, material pointed out by the learned counsel for the applicant,
delayed FIR and the fact that her statement has been recorded, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail,
hence the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Court for his appearance before the Trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the Trial Court during the pendency of trial.
It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437 (3) of Cr.P.C.
This application is allowed and stands disposed of.
Certified copy, as per Rules.

(SATYENDRA KUMAR SINGH) JUDGE (alok)
